theoryContent:
Principles of Energy Conservation in a Skate Park:
1. In the absence of non-conservative forces (Ideal Mode), total mechanical energy E = PE + KE remains constant at all times. As elevation increases, speed decreases to zero at the crest, and vice-versa.
2. At the lowest dip of the track, all available potential energy has converted into kinetic energy, yielding maximum speed v = √(2gΔy).
3. In Real mode, friction performs negative work on the skateboard wheels, converting mechanical energy into heat (thermal energy). However, the total energy of the closed system (PE + KE + Thermal) remains strictly conserved.
